title: Building the Taj Mahal: 20,000 Workers, 22 Years
description: How an emperor's grief became the world's most famous tomb.

scenes.narration: Twenty thousand workers. More than twenty years. All for one tomb.
scenes.image_prompt: thousands of workers building the Taj Mahal, wooden scaffolding around the white marble dome, Agra 1630s

scenes.narration: It's 1632, in Agra. Emperor Shah Jahan is grieving his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
scenes.image_prompt: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in royal robes standing sorrowfully at a palace window overlooking the Yamuna river

scenes.narration: He orders a tomb unlike anything the world has seen, on the bank of the Yamuna.
scenes.image_prompt: Mughal architects presenting building plans to the emperor in an ornate court, Persian carpets, lamps

scenes.narration: Masons, carvers and calligraphers come from across the empire and beyond.
scenes.image_prompt: Mughal craftsmen carving marble and writing Arabic calligraphy on stone panels in a busy workshop

scenes.narration: White marble is hauled from Makrana, in Rajasthan, hundreds of kilometres away.
scenes.image_prompt: long caravan of ox carts and elephants hauling huge white marble blocks across dusty Indian plains

scenes.narration: Around a thousand elephants are said to have carried materials.
scenes.image_prompt: many elephants carrying stone blocks along a riverbank construction site, the unfinished Taj Mahal rising behind

scenes.narration: Craftsmen set precious stones into the marble, flower by flower.
scenes.image_prompt: close up of artisan inlaying red and green gemstones into white marble in floral patterns, fine detail

scenes.narration: The main tomb was finished around 1643. Which building should we visit next? Comment below.
scenes.image_prompt: the completed Taj Mahal glowing at sunrise, reflection in the long water channel, gardens
